comment: “Export” suggests a direct LHR-to-user data-transfer model that is not appropriate for all secondary-use governance frameworks. Under the EHDS, processing for secondary use is permitted only for specified purposes and, in the ordinary access model, is authorised by a health data access body. Personal electronic health data are processed in secure processing environments, and personal data cannot be downloaded from those environments. The Reference Architecture should therefore treat secondary-use infrastructure as a distinct governance layer, rather than assuming that research and analytics platforms directly receive exports from the clinical LHR. This also makes the architecture compatible with federated health-data-space implementations.

public.suggestedRevision: Replace with: “Secondary-use data provision. The LHR shall support governed interfaces through which data necessary for legally authorised secondary purposes can be made available to the applicable secondary-use infrastructure. Where the legal framework provides for an access-authorisation body, data permit and/or secure processing environment, person-level data shall be routed through that mechanism rather than exported directly to secondary users or research applications.”
